name: Mozilla PDF.js
what_it_is: Mozilla's general-purpose, web-standards-based PDF parsing and rendering project. Its display layer exposes document, page rendering, text-content, text-layer, and annotation-layer APIs without requiring the full viewer UI.
render_model: Hybrid: PDFPageProxy.render paints page content to Canvas; TextLayer creates positioned transparent DOM text spans; AnnotationLayer creates positioned DOM/SVG/form elements for annotations represented by the PDF.
annotation_support: Reads and displays existing PDF annotations through getAnnotations and AnnotationLayer, and has selected editor/save support through AnnotationStorage. For jevsume's custom review objects, use overlay-only SVG/DOM state rather than PDF annotation dictionaries.
coordinate_space: PDF user space is exposed by PDFPageProxy.view; PageViewport transforms it to top-left viewport/canvas coordinates with scale, rotation, offsets, userUnit, and Y flip. In 6.3.289 convert rectangles with two convertToViewportPoint calls because convertToViewportRectangle was removed.
desktop_fit: Strong: direct page-to-canvas rendering, HiDPI output scaling, selectable text layer, optional native annotation layer, and viewport transforms fit a custom desktop React preview.
mobile_fit: Good [uncertain]: the same viewport/page-space model is usable at responsive scales, but gesture arbitration, render scheduling, memory limits, and transient pinch behavior require separate mobile validation.
overlay_chat_fit: Strong: stack jevsume's SVG review layer as a sibling above the canvas/text/native-annotation layers, keep anchors in PDF page space, and project them through the current PageViewport.
already_in_repo: Yes. package.json declares pdfjs-dist ^6.3.289; src/lib/extract.ts configures the Vite-emitted worker URL, loads PDF bytes, calls getTextContent per page, and flattens TextItem.str values for Jev.
risks: TextItem boundaries and normalized whitespace do not guarantee direct equality with Jev's flattened offsets; correct layer CSS and z-order are required; render tasks need cancellation/serialization; PDF.js AnnotationStorage is a custom format and is not a general programmatic PDF-annotation API.
recommendation: use — retain PDF.js as the rendering and text-geometry engine, use its native annotation layer only for PDF-owned links/forms/annotations, and keep jevsume review/chat/triggers in a separate application SVG overlay.
uncertain: Mobile performance and gesture behavior are not established by this desktop-focused task and need device-level research.
Reliable mapping from Jev character offsets to PDF.js TextItem geometry remains document-dependent and belongs to the span-to-glyph task.
